Copilot: these are the kit's agent rules, the same ones Claude Code reads. Where they name Claude Code tools, use the Copilot equivalent:

- Slash commands (/brd, /plan, ...): the prompts in .github/prompts/, run in Agent mode as /kit-brd, /kit-plan and so on (Copilot has its own /plan, /fix and /review). The text after the command name is my input for that step.
- The modeling MCP (powerbi-authoring): the tools of Microsoft's Power BI Modeling MCP extension for VS Code, server `powerbi-authoring-local`. If its tools aren't available, stop and ask me to start it (MCP: List Servers) and tick its tools (docs/COPILOT.md); never change the model another way. daxlib-mcp: the server in .mcp.json, or the vendored copy (design/udf/README.md).
- Claude Code agents and skills (reports:svg-reviewer, the pbip-validator agent, Data Goblins skills): not available. Review SVG measures yourself against .claude/rules/svg.md and validate with `pbik validate`.
- Run commands in the terminal from the project root; PowerShell scripts with `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ...`.

# pbip-kit

Goal: build polished Power BI reports (PBIP + PBIR) from a requirements file (design/reference/brd.md) and HTML wireframes. Public data only.

## Rules
- Canvas 1920x1080 (custom page size), 32px margin, 12-column grid, 24px gutters. Compute positions from the grid.
- Read design/tokens.json before styling. Never hardcode colors or fonts.
- Use only the powerbi-authoring modeling MCP server for model changes, plus the daxlib-mcp server (.mcp.json) only to
  install the DAX Lib packages listed in design/udf/packages.json, at `/model approved`. Ignore Fabric-only tools.
- Don't change the semantic model, or delete files, without asking.
- Running /model approved, /build or /fix counts as permission to commit; otherwise commit only when I say so.
- Approval gates: brd.md after /brd, the /model approval list, and /build approved after I have reviewed the wireframe.
- What the agent may see: aggregates only unless cleared (docs/it-security.md).
- Build, validate and check through pbik (tools/pbik/README.md): `python tools/pbik/pbik.py <command>` (or `pbik` after
  `pip install --user -e tools\pbik`). pbik rules and Desktop quirks are in .claude/rules/pbik.md.
- pbik is the only report CLI. Some installed Data Goblins skills show commands for another CLI: use their knowledge, but do the step with pbik or pbi-bridge.ps1. If pbik can't do it, stop and tell me.
- GitHub Copilot mirrors these files (.github/copilot-instructions.md, .github/prompts/): after editing CLAUDE.md,
  .claude/rules or .claude/commands, run `python tools/copilot/sync.py` (tests and doctor.ps1 check it).
- Plugin versions are pinned (auto-update off). At the start of each session, compare the installed plugin versions (~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json) with VERSIONS.md. If they differ, add a row to the changelog in VERSIONS.md with the date, the plugin, the old and new version, and a note to run /smoke (one card, one button slicer, one table) before building anything large.

## Accessibility
- Alt text, WCAG 2.1 AA contrast in every state, no text below 10pt, tab order in reading order: lessons A-01 to A-05
  (docs/lessons/accessibility.md), all warned on by `pbik validate`. Fix in layout.json, or note the exception by ID.

## Native first
- Build with native Power BI visuals and settings. Use SVG measures, HTML or custom visuals only as
  a fallback when a native visual can't do it (for example, status pill chips inside a table column).
- Visual-method ladder: 1 native (incl. the page background), 2 SVG (a measure, or a static image), 3 Deneb (certified
  AppSource visual), 4 any other custom visual (.pbiviz, HTML Content; uncertified until checked, docs/it-security.md).
  /plan picks the lowest step that meets the design (docs/patterns/ gives the ladder per pattern) and records
  `build.step` and `build.reason` per visual ID; audit_ids.py checks that the step matches `build.method`.
- Before using a fallback, tell me in one line what native option you tried and why it fails, record it in
  layout.json (`build.nativeTried`, `build.reason`) and in the fallback register in the spec by visual ID, and ask me
  before building it.
- Keep fallback work (like an SVG map) in place but unused until the native option is confirmed
  everywhere, then propose removing it.
- SVG rules are in .claude/rules/svg.md (a listed DAX Lib package before new SVG code). Deneb fallbacks and
  `build.method` are checked by `pbik validate` and audit_ids.py (docs/lessons/build.md).

## Visual IDs
- Every visual has a stable ID `P<page>-V<nn>` in layout.json, never reused: a removed visual's ID goes to `retired`.
- Use the ID in the wireframe (`data-id`), the spec, the review, the fix notes and the visual folder name (`<ID>_<name>`).
- Number visual IDs in reading order (top to bottom, left to right) so tab order follows: pbik writes tab order as the
  visual number x 100. Where it can't follow (a visual added later), set `tabOrder` on that visual in layout.json (Rep 9).
- design/scripts/audit_ids.py and `pbik validate --layout` check the IDs; /plan, /build, /review and /fix run them.

## Workflow
0. `/brd`: draft design/reference/brd.md from the template and my brief. Wait for my review.
1. `/model`: profile the raw data in data/ (row counts, timings, an audit-mode recommendation) and propose the core model from brd.md. Wait for my approval before applying it; `/model approved` applies it through the Modeling MCP, recalculates, runs `pbik model check` and a DAX query that every new measure returns a value, and commits.
2. `/plan`: first the design ambition in design/specs/spec.md (per key number: baseline, normal, exceptions, partial or stale; every headline number needs a comparison) and the patterns from docs/patterns/ that show it; then update design/tokens.json, write design/specs/layout.json, design/specs/spec.md and design/specs/audit.json. A wireframe or reference image in design/reference/ (any layout style: grid, bento, rail, tabs, dense tables) is optional input; if there is one, it is the source for layout.json (design/scripts/ref_layout.py), with what Power BI can't reproduce listed by ID. Otherwise layout.json comes from the BRD and design/scripts/gen_wireframe_hf.py draws the high-fidelity wireframe in design/wireframes/ (gen_wireframe.py, the box wireframe, is the fallback).
3. `/build`: build with `pbik build` from layout.json (styling through the theme and tokens), then run `pbik validate`, design/scripts/audit_layout.py and design/scripts/audit_ids.py.
4. I save and reload in Desktop; `/review` screenshots, compares to the wireframe and design/checks.md, and runs the numbers audit.
5. `/fix`: fix the review items, re-check, repeat.
6. `/wrapup` after the last /fix: places the rep's lessons (docs/lessons/README.md), updating existing ones, shows the diff, waits for approval; it suggests `/tidy` when a budget is near or 3+ reps have passed.
7. After each step, say what changed.
- `/theme` makes the colour scheme on its own (brand colours, a reference, or a preset: clean, bento, corporate;
  every text and state AA); /plan step 2 runs the same.
- `/smoke` after any tool or plugin update; `/update` after a Power BI Desktop update (docs/UPDATE-ROUTINE.md);
  `/validate` runs the numbers audit on its own.

## Audit modes
The numbers audit runs in full, sampled or aggregate-only mode (aggregate-only, with no row export, whenever
row-level access isn't cleared): /model recommends one and records it in design/reviews/model-check.md and design/specs/audit.json. The
modes, their provisional thresholds and what every mode keeps are in docs/lessons/audit-modes.md.

## Lessons
When a fix works, propose a lesson where docs/lessons/README.md places it (a check first; here only if it applies to
every session; one in, one out) and wait for approval. Lessons are Rule / Why / Enforced by / Source with an ID, in
docs/lessons/<topic>.md (dax, build, cards, slicers, charts, accessibility, audit-modes), each with an index; update a
lesson rather than add a duplicate, and never put a PROJECT-ONLY lesson in the kit. `python tools/lessons.py check`
(in the tests) enforces the format and the budgets. `/tidy` merges, retires and flags, never deletes.
pbik and Desktop quirks are in .claude/rules/pbik.md, SVG in .claude/rules/svg.md, and every gap with its Desktop click
steps in design/known-gaps.md (the pre-pbik gaps are history in examples/known-gaps-pbir.md).

### Desktop, refresh and reload
- Refresh is allowed when the source files exist in data/. Never repoint a source, and never refresh a model whose source is missing. A Calculate-only recalculation is always allowed.
- After adding calculated columns or tables, run a Calculate-only recalculation (it reads no data source). If it fails with "base version must not be negative", reconnect the modeling MCP first.
- Never reload or refresh while Desktop shows unsaved changes. Check first (`pbik desktop state --fail-if-dirty`) and stop if it's dirty; `pbik desktop reload` refuses on its own.
- After the agent edits report files, and after any reload or refresh (it marks the report unsaved itself), close Desktop without saving and reopen before the next reload.

# Rules: connect-pbid (.claude/rules/connect-pbid.md)

Learnings from Claude about connecting to semantic models via the connect-pbid skill

- Desktop Bridge params must be wrapped: `params = { client, args: { ... } }`. Flat params (as in references/desktop-bridge.md) fail; `args` is required even when empty.
- `file.reload/v1` defaults `reloadModelDefinition` to true; always pass false for report-only reloads.
- `report.snapshot.capture/v2` exists and accepts an optional `region` {x,y,width,height} in PBIR page units; useful for per-visual comparison.
- `report.snapshot.capture/v1` returns the visible canvas viewport (incl. collapsed Filters pane strip and scrollbar), not a clean page-only render.
- Client script for this project: `.claude/scripts/pbi-bridge.ps1` (manifest | state | reload | screenshot).

# Rules: pbik (.claude/rules/pbik.md)

pbik rules (tools/pbik/README.md has every command) and the Desktop and PBIR facts that came with them.

## Running pbik
- Run `python tools/pbik/pbik.py <command>` from the project root (no install), `tools\pbik\pbik.cmd`, or `pbik` after
  `pip install --user -e tools\pbik`.
- Drive builds from layout.json: it carries everything structured (PowerShell 5.1 strips quotes from JSON arguments,
  so never pass JSON on the command line). There is no per-rep build.py since pbik 0.6.
- `pbik build` is idempotent: run it twice and the second run must print "No changes". It writes only files whose content
  changes, so a clean `git diff` after a rerun is the check.
- Visuals without an ID (`P<n>-V<nn>_` folder) are never touched by `pbik build`; `pbik validate` reports them as errors.
- Properties pbik wrote and that left layout.json are removed on the next build, from the list in
  design/specs/visual-map.json (`owned`). Don't edit that file; if it's lost, the next build still sets everything,
  but properties dropped from layout.json in the meantime stay until `--reset`.
- `pbik build --reset` rebuilds each visual from its template, so Desktop-made changes inside ID'd visuals are lost:
  ask first.
- Schema checks use the cache in tools/pbik/schemas/ (`pbik schemas fetch <Report>`, git-ignored). Microsoft doesn't
  publish every version Desktop writes (visualContainer 2.14.0 is a 404); those files get a "not cached" warning.
- design/specs/project.json `targetDesktop` caps the `$schema` versions pbik writes to what that Desktop supports
  (Microsoft's published schema CHANGELOGs, tools/pbik/schema-support.json); validate errors on newer ones. Its
  `catalog` names the settings catalog validate warns from. Never change the target without asking
  (docs/UPDATE-ROUTINE.md).
- `pbik desktop reload` refuses while Desktop has unsaved changes and reloads the report only, never the model
  (`reloadModelDefinition` false). Exit code 3 means the bridge isn't available: that is "not checked", not "clean".

## When the Desktop Bridge is missing (exit 3; tools/doctor.ps1 says so)
- Nothing else changes: build and validate run on disk. Put the reload in the numbered Desktop click list as manual
  steps instead of running `pbik desktop reload`: 1. In Desktop, File > Close (don't save). 2. Open
  `<Report>.pbip` again from File Explorer. 3. Check the title bar shows no unsaved mark before going on.
- Screenshots: ask me for one PNG per page at 100% zoom (View > Page view > Actual size; Win+Shift+S), saved to
  `_snapshots/<page>.png`, instead of `pbik desktop screenshot`. Note "screenshots by hand, not page-exact" in
  review.md; skip the fidelity check ("Fidelity check: skipped (no Desktop Bridge)").

## Desktop and PBIR facts
- Desktop flags the report "unsaved" after opening and after every reload. Never reload while it's unsaved: close
  without saving and reopen first.
- Page-only screenshots: `pbik desktop screenshot --report <Report> --page <display name> --out <png> --region 0,0,1920,1080`
  (bridge capture v2), no Filters strip.
- Page-navigation buttons target the page **name** (the page.json `name`, a hex id), not the display name; pbik writes
  the name and `pbik validate` flags a display name.
- Filter values must be typed like the column: `2024L` (whole number), `1.5D` (decimal number), `'text'`. A number
  written as text never matches; pbik types values from the TMDL and validate flags text numbers.
- Desktop test round 1 (2026-10-17), from the Rep 4-7 files Desktop saved: button `text` / `fill` / `outline` / `icon`
  formatting sits on `{id: default}` with `show` selector-less, or Desktop ignores it (pbik does this for `props`); a
  bar chart's fx colour is per data point (data wildcard, no column metadata); a horizontal bar chart's value-axis line
  is `y1AxisReferenceLine`; table column widths are `columnWidth` on the column's metadata; the theme's slicer
  `data.mode` Dropdown needs `slicerMode` on the visual for a list. On save Desktop adds `active: true` to the first
  category field and drops `isDefaultSort: false`; pbik writes both the same way.
- Bookmarks (Rep 5, as Desktop saved them): `options.targetVisualNames` with `applyOnlyToTargetVisuals`, and
  `suppressActiveSection` so applying one doesn't switch page; display bookmarks add `suppressData`, a reset of the
  pane slicers is a data bookmark with `suppressDisplay` and nothing saved. A hidden visual is
  `singleVisual.display.mode: "hidden"` under its page's section. A button's bookmark is the bookmark id, not its
  display name.
- Report extension measures (reportExtensions.json) are bound with `SourceRef.Schema = "extension"`; an ImageUrl measure
  needs `dataType` Text.
- No PBIR property hides the table sort indicator; it sits at the left edge of a right-aligned sorted column.
- cardVisual per-field objects in the theme need `"$id": "default"`; set `layout.calloutSize` (75) or the aboveValue
  label clips.
- A conditional-formatting rule on a cardVisual `referenceLabelDetail.detailFontColor` with a wildcard selector doesn't
  render (tables render the same rules fine). Use a hex-returning measure on the detail colour instead (the measure must
  be in the TMDL first).
- Table per-column header alignment: `columnFormatting` on the field's `metadata` selector with `alignment` and
  `styleHeader: true`; `columnHeaders` per field is ignored. Theme `total.totals: false` didn't hide totals; set it on
  the visual (`props: {"total.totals": false}`).
- A theme change shows in Desktop after a report reload; there is no need to reopen.
- report.json (layout `report`: filter pane, report settings) isn't applied by Desktop's reload during the preview
  (Learn, external editing, 2026-09-29): close without saving and reopen; `pbik build` says so when it changed.
  Automatic filters reach visual.json only after the filter pane has been opened once, so with a collapsed pane
  they may never be saved: expected, and `pbik roundtrip` labels them `pane`, not as fixes. Desktop saves them with
  no `howCreated` and no condition (name, field, type), not `howCreated: Auto` (smoke save, 2026-11-10).
- Deneb (Patterns page save, 2026-10-24): `visualType` deneb7E15AEF80B9E4D4F8E12924291ECE89A, fields on the
  `dataset` role, the spec as one string in `vega.jsonSpec`, `stateManagement` beside it, and report.json
  `publicCustomVisuals` listing the visual. The saved file has no Deneb version, provider or config: the version shows
  only in Desktop (the visual's About). pbik writes Vega-Lite specs only.

# Rules: svg (.claude/rules/svg.md)

SVG and images: rules from Reps 2-7. SVG is a fallback (CLAUDE.md "Native first"): record the native option tried, the
reason, and a fallback register row before building one.

## Static SVG images (icons, court lines, wallpaper)
- Render each SVG to a transparent PNG at 4x its size with `design/scripts/svg_to_png.py` (headless Edge); full-canvas
  images at 1x (`--scale 1`). PNG is the route tested in Desktop; `pbik resource add` also takes an .svg, but that is
  not yet confirmed in Desktop.
- Register each PNG once with `pbik resource add <Report> <png>`; it reuses the
  same name instead of adding `<stem>_<digits>.png` copies.
- Bind it as `general.imageUrl` = `ResourcePackageItem` (PackageName RegisteredResources, PackageType 1, ItemName),
  `pbik_helpers.image_objects()`.

## SVG measures (DAX returning `data:image/svg+xml;utf8,...`, dataCategory ImageUrl)
- Write `%` inside the SVG as `%25` (`pbik validate` flags a raw one). A raw `%` (text such as "24%") stops Power BI decoding the data URI: every `%23`
  colour draws black while the text still shows (Rep 5).
- Show an SVG measure in a new card (filtered to one value, value and label hidden, image area 100, fit) or a table
  or matrix column (layout.json `cf` type `image`). An image visual can't take a measure.
- An extension measure references model measures only, never another extension measure (docs/lessons/dax.md).
- The card image needs a measure with a declared Text type: wrap the model measure in a report extension measure
  (`pbik measure ext add <Report> "img X" --expression "[Model Measure]" --data-category ImageUrl`).
- Test new SVG measures query-scoped first (`DEFINE MEASURE`), then write them to the TMDL.
- Every SVG measure must pass `design/scripts/audit_svg.py` (well-formed XML, no raw `%`) in every state of
  `design/specs/audit.json`, including the empty case and the first year.
- The numbers drawn in the SVG text are part of the numbers audit: `design/scripts/audit_numbers.py` (`svg` entries)
  compares them with `FORMAT ( [measure], "<format>" )`.
- Use a DAX Lib package listed in `design/udf/packages.json` (DaxLib.SVG) before writing a new SVG measure; it is
  installed at `/model approved` through daxlib-mcp (design/udf/README.md).
- DaxLib.SVG takes colours as raw `"#RRGGBB"`, unlike hand-written SVG. Its output keeps a raw `%` (`width='100%'`),
  so Power BI doesn't decode the URI: raw `#` colours render, `%23` colours draw nothing. Checked in Desktop on a card
  image and table images (v0.4.1, Rep 10 scratch). `pbik validate` flags a `%23` passed to DaxLib.SVG; the `%25` rule
  below is for SVG text you write yourself.
- Review SVG measures with the `reports:svg-reviewer` agent before building them.
